title: Frozen broker protocol version, closed vocabularies, bounded framing, hostile-frame refusal sweep
description:
SPIDR child 3b of 4, split from task-af3d7bc8af2146cf92d98557ed0e90c0 by architect-5aba94da. Human confirmed the 4-way split in the REPL. Carries parent DoD item 1, and the "refusal frames carry only op+code" half of parent DoD item 3.

DEPENDS ON task-05bf0e0fe7e84afb8584588ecf96db14 (3a: workspace wiring, broker package, descriptor acquisition). Do not start until 3a is DONE, and RE-MEASURE its landed symbols before planning rather than trusting this description -- every prior task in this chain found at least one stale claim in its own description.

Objective: define the wire contract and make it refuse everything malformed BEFORE any Job or process exists. This child is the reason the parent split cleanly: it needs no pipes, no Job, no process and no real Windows -- it is pure, fast, and exhaustively testable in isolation.

Deliverable, inside packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/broker/:
- src/frames.rs (NEW): bounded binary framing for fd0 (inbound control) and fd1 (outbound status), plus the bounded non-authoritative fd2 diagnostics form. Every length is checked against an explicit maximum before allocation. A frame that would exceed the cap is refused without allocating to its declared size -- a declared length is attacker-controlled and must never be trusted as an allocation hint.
- src/control.rs (NEW): the frozen protocol version and the CLOSED control vocabulary -- exactly one launch request shape and CANCEL. No catch-all variant, no open string command space.
- src/status.rs (NEW): the CLOSED status vocabulary -- STARTED with its identity payload, terminal COMPLETED, and REFUSED. A refusal frame carries only the exact stable operation and numeric Win32 code; it can carry no executable, argv, cwd, environment or handle data and no free-form error string, and the TYPE must make that unrepresentable rather than merely unwritten.
- tests/frame_sweep.rs (NEW): the hostile-frame sweep.

The parent DoD names six hostile classes explicitly and all six must be covered: malformed, truncated, reordered, duplicate, extra, and over-limit. Each must refuse BEFORE the lifecycle core would create a Job or process -- that ordering is the point, not merely that a refusal happens.

The sweep must assert a NONZERO EXACT generated-case count. A generated sweep that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing; that defect has been found on this board before, and epic rail 6 names it. Cross-check the produced refusal-reason set against the production vocabulary rather than against the sweep's own case list.

NOT IN SCOPE: descriptor acquisition (3a), Job creation, process launch, lifecycle delegation, STARTED emission timing, completion semantics (3c), idempotence or kill proofs (3d). No JavaScript, no daemon/store, no receipts, no public @moe/runner export.

Verification: cargo test --locked --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-broker && cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-broker
definitionOfDone: A frozen protocol version constant and CLOSED control, status and refusal-reason vocabularies exist as enums with no catch-all variant and no open string space, so adding a case is a compile error at every match site. The version is asserted by an exact-equality test, and a frame declaring any other version is refused by its own stable reason code.

Framing is bounded on all three of fd0, fd1 and fd2. A declared length exceeding the cap is refused WITHOUT allocating to the declared size, proved by a test that submits an enormous declared length and asserts the specific over-limit reason code rather than relying on the absence of a crash.

All six hostile classes the parent names are covered by the sweep -- malformed, truncated, reordered, duplicate, extra, and over-limit -- each asserting its own exact stable reason code, never merely that the frame was rejected. Where two layers could refuse, the test pins WHICH layer refused.

Every hostile case is proved to refuse BEFORE any Job or process would be created, asserted as the absence of any lifecycle-core call in a recorded call log -- not merely that an error was returned. Ordering is the requirement, not the outcome.

The sweep asserts a NONZERO EXACT generated-case count, so a generator that silently produces zero cases fails, and cross-checks the produced refusal-reason set against the production vocabulary rather than against its own case list. Verified by deleting one production reason and confirming the suite goes red.

A REFUSED frame is structurally incapable of carrying an executable path, argv, cwd, environment, handle value or free-form error string -- unrepresentable in the type, not merely absent from current call sites, so a future field addition fails to compile rather than leaking.

Every Rust production source is <=250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` with counts recorded; the locked broker test and release build both exit 0; no executable, Cargo target output, transcript or generated smoke evidence is committed.
taskRails: Control and status use bounded binary framing on fd0/fd1; fd2 diagnostics is bounded and non-authoritative. A declared length is attacker-controlled input and must never be used as an allocation hint before it is bounds-checked.

Closed vocabularies only: no catch-all enum variant, no open command string space, no free-form error text anywhere in a frame. Refusals carry the stable operation and numeric Win32 code and nothing else, enforced by the type.

Refuse before authority: every malformed, truncated, reordered, duplicate, extra or over-limit frame must be rejected before the lifecycle core would create a Job or process, and the test must assert the absence of the core call, not just the error.
Import moe-windows-job-core for its reason vocabulary rather than restating operation codes; do not duplicate its Win32 authority.
Keep every Rust production source focused, target and hard-cap <=250 physical lines; split before 400. Never commit Cargo target output, binaries, transcripts or smoke evidence.

Do not implement descriptor acquisition, Job creation, process launch, lifecycle delegation, STARTED timing, completion semantics, idempotence or kill proofs. Those belong to SPIDR siblings 3a, 3c and 3d.

implementationPlan.description: THE SHARED PROTOCOL VOCABULARY. Create broker/src/protocol.rs holding three things and nothing else. (1) A frozen `PROTOCOL_VERSION` constant. (2) `ProtocolReason`, a CLOSED enum with no catch-all, one variant per refusal this task can produce -- at minimum: version mismatch, opcode unknown, length over limit, frame truncated, trailing bytes after a frame, duplicate launch, frame out of order, and payload malformed. Give it an `ordinal()` accessor exactly as DescriptorReason has one. (3) `ProtocolError { reason, code }` with accessors only -- copy DescriptorError's shape: NO String field, NO path, NO argv, NO handle. A future field addition of that kind must fail to compile, which is what DoD item 6 means by unrepresentable. DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM DescriptorReason: descriptor and protocol refusals are different layers, and merging them would make 'which layer refused' unassertable, since a refusal migrating between layers would keep both suites green.
implementationPlan.note:
protocol.rs landed, 205 lines, `cargo check` exit 0. Holds exactly the three things the step names and nothing else.

(1) `PROTOCOL_VERSION: u8 = 1`, frozen, documented as checked before opcode, length or payload.
(2) `ProtocolReason`, CLOSED, 10 variants, no catch-all, no `#[non_exhaustive]`, with `ALL: [ProtocolReason; 10]` (length in the type) and `ordinal()` copied from DescriptorReason's shape. Variants: VersionMismatch, LengthOverLimit, FrameTruncated, ChannelFailed, UnknownOpcode, PayloadMalformed, TrailingBytes, DuplicateLaunch, FrameOutOfOrder, FrameAfterTerminal. That is the step's required eight plus two the step's own later steps force: ChannelFailed (step 4 needs a reason when the injected byte channel itself fails, and it is the only reason whose `code` is a real OS error rather than 0 — without it `code` would be vestigially always-zero) and FrameAfterTerminal (step 7 explicitly requires EXTRA to have a distinct reason for trailing-bytes-inside-a-frame versus a-frame-after-the-terminal-one).
(3) `ProtocolError { reason, code }`, private fields, accessors only, hand-written Display. Deliberately SEPARATE from DescriptorReason, per the step and planningNotes.

STRENGTHENING BEYOND THE STEP, both cheap and both serving DoD items already on the task:

A. `ProtocolStage { Framing, Control }` + `ProtocolReason::stage()` (exhaustive match, no `_` arm) + `ProtocolError::stage()`. DoD 3 says "Where two layers could refuse, the test pins WHICH layer refused". Descriptor-vs-protocol is pinned structurally by having two enums. But TWO LAYERS ALSO EXIST INSIDE the protocol -- framing (bytes) and control (meaning) -- and without a stage discriminant, moving e.g. the trailing-byte check from control into framing would keep every reason-code assertion green. Framing owns VersionMismatch, LengthOverLimit, FrameTruncated, ChannelFailed; Control owns UnknownOpcode, PayloadMalformed, TrailingBytes, DuplicateLaunch, FrameOutOfOrder, FrameAfterTerminal.

B. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE, disclosed because it moves a reason across the split the plan implied: UNKNOWN OPCODE IS A CONTROL-STAGE REASON, NOT A FRAMING ONE. Step 4 says "verify the version BEFORE parsing opcode or payload". Rather than merely ordering the two checks, the framing layer now never interprets the opcode at all -- it carries the byte through. That is strictly stronger for the ordering trap (a wrong-version frame cannot reach opcode interpretation because opcode interpretation is in a different module), and it is what lets ONE bounded codec serve fd0, fd1 and fd2 without embedding three vocabularies in the framing layer. Version-first is preserved and still directly tested in step 3.

C. DoD 6 ("unrepresentable, so a future field addition fails to compile") is enforced three ways rather than by comment: `derive(Copy)` -- every forbidden payload (String/PathBuf executable or cwd, Vec argv or env, String message) is non-Copy so the derive breaks; `derive(Debug)` -- the core's RawHandle deliberately has no Debug, so a handle field breaks it; and `const _: () = assert!(size_of::<ProtocolError>() == 8)` -- which fails the BUILD on any field addition at all, including a numeric one that would slip past the first two.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED: THE BOUNDED-FRAMING TESTS, before any codec exists. Create broker/tests/frame_sweep.rs with a scripted byte-channel double that can serve exact bytes, short reads and partial writes, and record everything written. Write the failing tests first: an enormous declared length (near u32::MAX) is refused with the exact over-limit reason AND the test is written so a regression that allocated first would exhaust memory rather than merely fail an assertion; a frame cut mid-header and one cut mid-payload each report truncated; a wrong version reports version mismatch; and -- the ordering trap -- a frame that is BOTH wrong-version and otherwise malformed reports the VERSION reason, proving the version check runs first and its reason is reachable. These must be pure unit-level tests over bytes: no pipe, no process, no Windows.
implementationPlan.note:
tests/frame_sweep.rs created with the scripted byte-channel double and 13 framing tests. RED VERIFIED, and for the right reason:

`error[E0432]: unresolved imports moe_windows_job_broker::read_frame, ::write_frame, ::ByteChannel, ::ChannelKind, ::RawFrame, ::FRAME_HEADER_BYTES` -> exit 101. The codec is missing; nothing here is a typo, and `ProtocolError`/`ProtocolReason`/`ProtocolStage`/`PROTOCOL_VERSION` resolved because step 2 landed them.

`Scripted` serves exact bytes, SHORT READS (`in_chunks_of`), PARTIAL WRITES (`accepting_writes_of`), injectable read/write failure codes, and records every byte written. Chosen over `std::io::Cursor` because a codec that assumed whole reads would pass against Cursor and corrupt frames against a real pipe.

Every test the step names is present:
- `a_declared_length_near_u32_max_is_refused_before_the_payload_is_read` -- declares u32::MAX-8 with six bytes supplied, asserts LengthOverLimit AND code()==0.
- `a_frame_cut_mid_header_reports_truncated` (3 bytes) and `a_frame_cut_mid_payload_reports_truncated` (declares 8, supplies 3).
- `a_wrong_version_byte_reports_version_mismatch`.
- THE ORDERING TRAP: `a_frame_that_is_both_wrong_version_and_over_limit_reports_the_version_reason` -- wrong version AND an undefined opcode AND ~4 GiB declared, all at once; only a version-first codec can answer VersionMismatch.

DELIBERATE STRENGTHENING OF THE STEP'S "no-allocation" PROOF. The step asks for a test "written so a regression that allocated first would exhaust memory rather than merely fail an assertion". Memory exhaustion is NOT a reliable detector on 64-bit Windows: `vec![0u8; 4GiB]` can succeed against the page file, after which the regression would report FrameTruncated and the test would still pass for an accidental reason. So the double counts bytes pulled and the test asserts `channel.bytes_read() == FRAME_HEADER_BYTES`. A codec that sized a buffer from the declaration would also have READ against it, so pinning the count to exactly the header is deterministic where an OOM is not. The ~4 GiB declaration is kept as the secondary signal.

Also added beyond the step, all cheap and all serving DoD 2: empty-channel -> FrameTruncated (EOF is not an empty frame); one-byte-at-a-time reads still decode; read failure -> ChannelFailed carrying the real numeric code (ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE 109); write accepted one byte at a time still emits every byte IN ORDER; write failure -> ChannelFailed with nothing recorded as sent; an over-cap payload is refused on the WRITE side too with not one byte emitted; and `each_of_the_three_channels_bounds_its_own_frames_at_its_own_cap`, which asserts the three caps are STRICTLY ORDERED fd2 < fd1 < fd0 and then submits one length that is over-limit on fd2 but merely truncated on fd0/fd1 -- that is what proves the cap is per channel rather than one global number, which a same-cap-everywhere implementation would pass vacuously.

`assert_refused` asserts the LITERAL expected stage rather than `reason.stage()`, so it pins the reason-to-layer mapping table instead of restating it.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN: THE BOUNDED CODEC. Create broker/src/frames.rs with a narrow byte-channel trait (read into a caller-owned buffer, write a slice) so the whole sweep runs injected, and the bounded frame reader/writer over it. Define one explicit maximum frame length as a named constant. CHECK THE DECLARED LENGTH AGAINST THE CAP BEFORE ALLOCATING ANYTHING -- never `Vec::with_capacity(declared)` ahead of the bound check; a declared length is attacker-controlled and that pattern is the memory-exhaustion bug DoD item 2 exists to catch. Verify the version BEFORE parsing opcode or payload so a future re-layout reports a version mismatch rather than malformed. Apply the same bounded form to the fd2 diagnostics frame, which is non-authoritative and must never be parsed as control. Do NOT reuse HandleCalls for I/O: it has only file_type and close_handle, no read or write, and contorting framing through it would be worse than a new narrow seam.

INBOUND CONTROL VOCABULARY AND THE ACCEPT STATE. Create broker/src/control.rs with the CLOSED inbound vocabulary: exactly one launch request shape and CANCEL, no catch-all, no open string command space. Decoding yields `Accepted::Launch(LaunchRequest)` or `Accepted::Cancel`, or a ProtocolError. LaunchRequest is the one type that legitimately carries the executable, argv, cwd and environment -- that is its purpose, and it is precisely why ProtocolError must not; keeping them separate is what makes the no-echo rail enforceable by construction rather than by discipline. REORDERED AND DUPLICATE ARE SEQUENCE PROPERTIES a stateless decoder cannot see, so add a minimal accept state -- expecting-launch versus already-launched -- so that a second launch is DUPLICATE and a CANCEL arriving before any launch is OUT OF ORDER, each with its own reason code. That state holds no Job, no handle and no process; it is not 3c's session and must not grow into one.

OUTBOUND STATUS VOCABULARY, INCLUDING THE LAYER DISCRIMINANT. Create broker/src/status.rs with the CLOSED outbound vocabulary: STARTED with its identity payload, terminal COMPLETED, and REFUSED. THREE LAYERS CAN NOW REFUSE -- descriptor (3a), protocol (this task) and native (the core, reaching the wire via 3c) -- so a REFUSED frame carrying only a number cannot tell a reader which one spoke. Carry an explicit `RefusalLayer` discriminant alongside the layer-local reason ordinal and the numeric code, so 'which layer refused' is assertable ON THE WIRE and not merely in Rust types. Native failures carry moe_windows_job_core's NativeOp and its numeric code rather than a restated operation vocabulary, per task rail 4. The REFUSED frame must be structurally incapable of holding an executable path, argv, cwd, environment, handle value or free-form string. Emitting STARTED and COMPLETED is 3c's job; this task defines and encodes them only.

COMPLETE THE HOSTILE SWEEP. Extend tests/frame_sweep.rs to cover ALL SIX classes the parent DoD names -- malformed, truncated, reordered, duplicate, extra, over-limit -- each asserting its OWN exact ProtocolReason, never merely that a frame was rejected. Fix the meaning of EXTRA before testing it: cover both trailing bytes after a well-formed frame and an unexpected additional frame after the terminal one, with a distinct reason for each rather than one case that silently tests neither. Assert a NONZERO EXACT case count so a generator producing zero cases fails. Cross-check the produced reason set against the production ProtocolReason vocabulary, not against the sweep's own case list. THE AUTHORITY PROOF (DoD item 4): assert that every hostile case returns Err with its exact reason AND produces NO `Accepted` value -- since a LaunchRequest is the only value that can ever reach a process launch, unconstructibility is a strictly stronger proof than an empty call log, which would be vacuously true here because nothing in this task can call the core at all. Add at least one BYTE-EXACT encoding assertion per status variant against a hand-written literal; an encode-then-decode round trip only proves two functions you wrote agree with each other.

WIRE UP AND AUDIT SIZE. In broker/src/lib.rs add `mod protocol; mod frames; mod control; mod status;` and re-export the public surface, keeping every item on exactly one public path as the existing comment requires. Update the lib.rs module doc to describe the protocol layer and to name which siblings still own what (3c session, 3d hardening). ADD NOTHING TO main.rs -- its module doc explicitly forbids even a placeholder for this task's work, on the grounds that a placeholder is a second implementation for its owner to collide with. Add nothing to descriptors.rs, which is at 222 of its 250 cap. Then audit every broker production source with `grep -c ''` and record each count: lib.rs, main.rs, boundary.rs, descriptors.rs, verify.rs, bin/handle_probe.rs, protocol.rs, frames.rs, control.rs, status.rs. Every one must be <=250; split by responsibility, never by reformatting, if any exceeds it.

VERIFY, ATTACK, COMMIT. (a) Run the task's exact verification command -- locked test AND locked release build for -p moe-windows-job-broker -- and paste real output; both exit 0. Re-run the CORE's verification command and confirm it is still green and unchanged. (b) Compare against the step-1 baseline; any repo-wide red must exist at the merge-base too or it is yours. (c) MUTATION DRILL, required by epic rail 6: move the length bound check to AFTER the allocation and confirm the over-limit test goes RED; move the version check to after opcode parsing and confirm the wrong-version-and-malformed test goes RED; delete one entry from ProtocolReason and confirm the vocabulary cross-check goes RED; change one byte of a status encoding and confirm the byte-exact assertion goes RED. Restore each and re-confirm green, verifying by reading file contents rather than trusting a clean git status, since a foreign whole-tree commit can capture a drill edit. (d) Adversarial pass: no ProtocolError, REFUSED frame or diagnostics frame can carry a path, argv, environment or handle; no decode path allocates on an unchecked length; the decoder cannot panic on any byte sequence. (e) IN THE COMPLETION NOTES, state explicitly that DoD item 4's 'recorded call log' form was satisfied by type-level unconstructibility instead, and why an empty core call log would have been vacuous here -- disclose the form change rather than letting QA discover it. (f) `git status --porcelain`, unstage anything foreign, commit by explicit pathspec over owned paths only, verify with `git show --stat`.

comments.content:
SEAM UPDATE from architect-5aba94da, 2026-08-10. Read before planning. This task's description was written before 3a existed; 3a has now landed and introduced structure the description does not anticipate.

PROVISIONAL: 3a (task-05bf0e0f) is in REVIEW, not DONE, 9/9 steps. QA may still reject and move things. Your unblock condition is unchanged -- wait for DONE -- and you must still re-measure. This comment tells you WHAT TO LOOK FOR so you do not design against the wrong shape.

THE BIG ONE: A CALL-TABLE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS. DO NOT BUILD A SECOND.
3a shipped `pub trait HandleCalls` in broker/src/verify.rs, with RAII types `OwnedDescriptor` and `Descriptors` generic over it, and the real implementation `SystemHandles` in broker/src/boundary.rs. This mirrors the core's Win32Calls/SystemWin32 pattern. Your framing and control modules must be injectable through THAT seam, not through a new parallel one. A second call table in the same crate is duplicated authority and will read as a rail violation.

THE BROKER IS A LIB + BIN, NOT JUST A BIN.
broker/src/lib.rs exists and re-exports everything; broker/src/main.rs is a thin entry point. Your frames/control/status modules are `mod` declarations in lib.rs with `pub use` re-exports, following the one-public-path convention the core crate documents. The description's "src/frames.rs (NEW)" etc. still holds -- just know they hang off lib.rs.

ALREADY EXPORTED, do not restate:
  parse_descriptor_block, DescriptorError, DescriptorReason, INVALID_HANDLE,
  REQUIRED_DESCRIPTOR_COUNT, acquire_from_block, Descriptors, HandleCalls,
  OwnedDescriptor, PIPE_FILE_TYPE, and (windows-only) acquire, startup_block, SystemHandles.

A CLOSED REFUSAL VOCABULARY ALREADY EXISTS: `DescriptorReason`. Your DoD requires closed control, status and refusal-reason vocabularies. DECIDE DELIBERATELY whether your protocol reasons EXTEND that enum or sit beside it as a separate closed enum composed into one error type. Do not create a second overlapping reason vocabulary by accident -- if two enums can both describe "refused", tests asserting a reason code stop pinning which layer refused, which is exactly the vacuous-assertion defect the global rail names.

PIPE_FILE_TYPE IS PINNED AND THE TRAP IS CLOSED. 3a defined `pub const PIPE_FILE_TYPE: u32 = 3` and guarded it with `const _: () = assert!(PIPE_FILE_TYPE == FILE_TYPE_PIPE)` in boundary.rs, so a wrong value fails the build. Reuse the constant; never write 2 or 3 as a literal. (FILE_TYPE_CHAR is 2, FILE_TYPE_PIPE is 3 -- I confirmed this empirically with a spawn probe before planning 3a.)

FILE LAYOUT AS LANDED (line counts by `grep -c ''`): src/lib.rs 51, src/main.rs 85, src/boundary.rs 94, src/bin/handle_probe.rs 127, src/verify.rs 157, src/descriptors.rs 222. All production sources are under the 250 cap, but descriptors.rs at 222 has little headroom -- do not add protocol code there. tests/: descriptor_block.rs 401, handle_inheritance.rs 446, node_loadability.rs 132 (test files are exempt; the cap is per PRODUCTION file).

Broker gate green at HEAD when I measured: 8 + 1 + 1 = 10 tests passing, 0 failed.

Same guidance applies to siblings task-55e2c4c8 (3c) and task-e18b1284 (3d); I am posting it here because you are next in the chain.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REFUSAL VOCABULARY: SEPARATE ENUM, NOT AN EXTENSION OF DescriptorReason. Rejected extending DescriptorReason with protocol cases. Descriptor refusals and protocol refusals are different layers, and the global rail requires a test to pin WHICH layer refused. One merged enum makes that unpinnable — a descriptor test and a protocol test would assert against the same vocabulary, so a refusal migrating between layers keeps both green. Chose a separate closed `ProtocolReason` plus `ProtocolError { reason, code }` mirroring DescriptorError's shape (accessors only, no string field).

THE WIRE MUST NAME THE LAYER. Because three layers can now refuse — descriptor (3a), protocol (this task), native (the core, via 3c) — a REFUSED frame that carries only a number cannot tell a reader which one spoke. Chose an explicit `RefusalLayer` discriminant on the frame alongside the layer-local reason ordinal and the numeric code. That is what makes 'which layer refused' assertable on the wire rather than only in Rust types, and it is why the frame does not simply reuse NativeOp for everything.

DoD ITEM 4 — READ THIS, IT IS THE ONE PLACE I AM DELIBERATELY DIVERGING IN FORM. The item says hostile frames must be proved to refuse 'asserted as the absence of any lifecycle-core call in a recorded call log'. This task has no session and never touches the core's Job or process constructors, so wiring a core recording double into the sweep and asserting it is empty would be VACUOUSLY true — nothing here could ever call it, which is exactly the detached-assertion defect the global rail names. Chose a STRICTLY STRONGER proof instead: make authority unreachable by TYPE. Decoding yields `Accepted::Launch(LaunchRequest)` or `Accepted::Cancel`, and a LaunchRequest is the ONLY value that can later reach a process launch. The sweep asserts that every hostile case returns Err with its exact reason AND that no Accepted value is produced. A call log can be satisfied by code that simply has not called yet; unconstructibility cannot. The literal call-log form becomes meaningful in 3c, whose DoD already requires it where the session actually holds the calls. THE WORKER MUST STATE THIS DIVERGENCE AND ITS REASONING EXPLICITLY IN THE COMPLETION NOTES so QA judges it knowingly — do not silently substitute.

I/O SEAM. Chose a narrow byte-channel trait (read into a caller-owned buffer, write a slice) defined in frames.rs, injectable so the whole sweep runs with no pipe, no process and no Windows. Rejected reusing HandleCalls (no read/write) and rejected std::io::Read/Write directly, because the sweep needs to script short reads and partial writes, which a bare Read impl makes awkward to assert against.

LaunchRequest CARRIES paths and argv; ProtocolError MUST NOT. These are not in tension: the launch REQUEST is the payload whose whole purpose is to carry an executable and arguments, while the REFUSAL is forbidden from echoing them. Keeping them in separate types is what makes the rail enforceable by construction.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE VACUOUS-ASSERTION TRAP IS THE MAIN RISK HERE, and it is subtle because the DoD's own wording invites it. If the worker adds a core recording double and asserts it is empty, that assertion is true for reasons unrelated to the code under test and will stay true forever, including after a real defect. See approachesConsidered; use the unconstructibility proof and disclose the form change.

2. A DECLARED LENGTH IS ATTACKER INPUT AND MUST NOT BE AN ALLOCATION HINT. `Vec::with_capacity(declared)` before the bound check is the classic memory-exhaustion bug and it is what DoD item 2 exists to catch. Bound-check first, allocate second, and make the over-limit test submit a length near u32::MAX so a regression would allocate gigabytes rather than merely failing an assert.

3. 'REORDERED' AND 'DUPLICATE' ARE SEQUENCE PROPERTIES, NOT SINGLE-FRAME PROPERTIES. A stateless decoder cannot detect either. This task therefore needs a small explicit accept-state (expecting-launch versus launched) so a second launch is DUPLICATE and a CANCEL before any launch is REORDERED, each with its own reason. Do not confuse that minimal state with 3c's session — it holds no Job, no handle and no process, only which frames are legal next.

4. 'EXTRA' NEEDS ITS MEANING FIXED BEFORE IT CAN BE TESTED: trailing bytes after a well-formed frame, or an unexpected additional frame after the terminal one. Both are real; pick one meaning per reason code and cover both behaviours, rather than leaving a case that silently tests neither.

5. THE VERSION CHECK MUST COME FIRST. If length or opcode parsing runs before the version check, a future version's re-layout is reported as malformed rather than as a version mismatch, and the version reason becomes unreachable. Test that a frame that is BOTH wrong-version and malformed reports the version reason.

6. Do not let a status ENCODER round-trip test stand in for a decoder test. Encoding then decoding your own output exercises agreement between two functions you wrote, not conformance to the frozen format. Pin at least one byte-exact expected encoding per status variant against a hand-written literal.

7. descriptors.rs is at 222 of 250 and main.rs's module doc forbids placeholders. Add nothing to either beyond the lib.rs module declarations and re-exports.

8. Shared working directory: commit by explicit pathspec over owned paths only, after `git status --porcelain` and unstaging anything foreign; verify with `git show --stat`. The crate's bytes have already been swept into foreign whole-tree commits three times on this chain.
